subject.title: Telegram: collapse mid-paragraph newlines before sending

question: Should Telegram collapse model-emitted single newlines inside prose/list items by default, expose an opt-in setting, or keep line preservation as the supported behavior?
rationale: Current code and recent rich-message work intentionally preserve single newlines, while a safe collapse path likely needs either a public config knob or an explicit default policy tradeoff.

options.title: Add opt-in collapse policy
options.body: Add a Telegram config option for Markdown-aware soft-wrap collapse, default it off, and document/test preserved blocks and rich/plain behavior.

options.title: Make collapse the default
options.body: Change Telegram output globally to collapse detected soft-wraps, accepting compatibility risk for users who rely on single-newline preservation.

options.title: Keep preservation behavior
options.body: Close this direction after maintainer confirmation that preserving model newlines is the intended Telegram behavior and point users to prompts or formatting guidance.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in collapse policy
recommendation.body: Add a Telegram config option for Markdown-aware soft-wrap collapse, default it off, and document/test preserved blocks and rich/plain behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible recent history across the Telegram formatter, send, config, and docs surfaces involved in the product/default decision.
